inventory.sourceFigureDescription: A rod-shaped bacterium with surface structures (capsular polysaccharide as wavy lines, M protein as rectangles, Protein A as surface structures); a phagocytosis cell with a blocked symbol; a complement-mediated phagocytosis cell interacting with Protein A bound to the Fc region of IgG (blocking the Fc receptor / opsonization); and IgA protease shown cleaving IgA. (The source's own typo 'Completment-mediated phagocytosis' is printed in this diagram.)

inventory.visualPurpose: Resistance — the antibiotic resistance mechanisms figure
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: A bacterial-cell schematic with three mechanism columns: INCREASED EFFLUX/DECREASED UPTAKE (tetracyclines, sulfonamides, fluoroquinolones); ENZYMATIC INACTIVATION with drug cleavage (penicillin G, V; penicillinase-sensitive penicillins; cephalosporins; carbapenems) and drug modification (aminoglycosides, chloramphenicol); and DRUG TARGET MODIFICATION with rRNA (linezolid, macrolides), enzyme (penicillinase-resistant penicillins; cephalosporins; sulfonamides; fluoroquinolones), and cell wall (vancomycin) — the cell carrying anatomy labels (BACTERIAL CELL, cell wall, ribosome with rRNA, mRNA, DNA, enzyme).
